reports.title: Maximus Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year Results for Fiscal Year 2026

guidance.heading: Fiscal Year 2027 Guidance
section: Maximus is establishing fiscal year 2027 guidance.

We expect revenue to range between $5.45 billion and $5.65 billion. The outlook includes approximately ten months of contribution from Agile Defense and reflects expectations for continued growth opportunities across defense and national security markets, state government programs, and technology-enabled services.
Maximus expects adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 12.8% for fiscal year 2027 and adjusted diluted earnings per share to range between $7.50 and $8.00 per share.

This guidance assumes no incentive contribution related to the VA MDE contracts during fiscal year 2027. Fiscal year 2026 included incentive-related revenue and profit equal to an estimated $75 million and $1.05 adjusted earnings per share, respectively, total contribution across the first three quarters of the fiscal year 2026. Excluding the incentive contribution related to the VA MDE contracts to the fiscal year 2026, the midpoint of our adjusted diluted earnings per share guidance represents growth of approximately 8%.

We expect free cash flow to range between $700 million and $800 million. The outlook reflects DSO returning to the historical range of 60-70 days and includes the benefit of collections that shifted beyond fiscal year-end.

For fiscal year 2027, Maximus expects amortization of intangible assets of approximately $96 million, depreciation and amortization of property, equipment and capitalized software of approximately $55 million, interest expense of approximately $110 million, an effective tax rate of approximately 25%, and weighted average shares outstanding of approximately 52.1 million.

desk.headline: Revenue down 1% to $1.30bn, in line; adjusted EPS $2.11 beat; FY27 outlook set at $5.45–5.65bn revenue, $7.50–8.00 adjusted EPS

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted diluted (excl. intangible amortisation and divestiture items); GAAP diluted EPS was $1.83 vs $1.32

results: Quarterly sales slipped 1% to $1.30bn, close to estimates, while adjusted EPS jumped 30% to $2.11 and GAAP EPS rose to $1.83 from $1.32.
Margins widened: adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 14.6% from 12.2%, helped by automation and cost control; the federal unit's margin hit 19.8%.
Full year: revenue $5.23bn (down 4%, inside guidance) and adjusted EPS $8.24, above the top of guidance; about $1.05 of that came from VA incentive payments that will not recur.
Cash was weak for the year (free cash flow $69m) as a big customer paid late; more than $330m was collected after year-end.
About $192m of shares were bought back in FY26; the $0.33 quarterly dividend continues. The Agile Defense deal closed on 18 Nov, lifting pro forma leverage to about 2.3x.

guidance.summary: Maximus set its first fiscal 2027 outlook, including about ten months of Agile Defense. It assumes no VA MDE incentive income, which added about $1.05 to FY26 adjusted EPS, so EPS is guided slightly lower than FY26.

points: Agile Defense is expected to bring about $450m of revenue in calendar 2027; CEO Bruce Caswell called it "a growth story".
The new VA medical exam contract will run five years instead of ten, with bids due in mid-December and a start on 1 July 2027; that change cut the pipeline by about $5.6bn to $44.8bn.
Medicaid work-requirement and eligibility work is picking up, with five states signed; SNAP is seen as a growth area.
Management expects most of the delayed cash to arrive in FY27 and plans about $200m of buybacks; Q1 is expected to be the weakest quarter.
Overseas markets (Gulf and UK) remain under pressure, and government customers are still cautious about adopting AI.
